item-0009.final_summary: Implemented by 7546fca (2026-06-16), 'feat(verify): seal the CT log into the golden trusted root', which predates the item store -- the item was transcribed from docs/ROADMAP-sigstore-test-harness.md without noticing the work had landed, and is closed retroactively after verification on 2026-08-19. Verified: the golden ctlogs entry carries logId.keyId = base64(sha256(DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo)) of its embedded key, recomputed independently, and that key is byte-identical to the harness pki/ctfe-pub.pem SPKI (PKIX_ECDSA_P256_SHA_256, SHA2_256). The Rekor tlogs logId uses the C2SP signed-note derivation and is not sha256(SPKI), so the two log ids are distinct as required. 7546fca regenerated exactly the four goldens (sealed, engine-context, informational, trusted_root). The golden-consuming tests pass with no external network, confirmed by running internal/verify and the cmd/strike verify tests inside an isolated network namespace. Caveat on the 'Rekor entry unchanged' clause: the Rekor key and Fulcio chain did change in that commit because the harness was cold-started between generations, which the item body anticipates; the clause holds in its intended sense, that the Rekor derivation was left untouched while ctlogs was added. Corroboration: ctlogs survived four later golden regenerations (e7d2efd, f872d43, 1da3a0b, 4ef9b63), still matches the live harness key, and cosign verifies the embedded SCT against it with no insecure flag.

item-0010.final_summary: Implemented by 386dba2 (2026-06-16), 'feat(harness): add flag-clean cosign conformance target', landed the same day as the item-0009 commit and likewise predating the item store; closed retroactively after verification on 2026-08-19. Verified: the conformance target at test/sigstore-local/Makefile verifies all three golden bundles offline with cosign v3.1.1 and carries no --insecure-* flag (the only 'insecure' match in the file is the echo banner). SCT enforcement was falsification-tested rather than assumed -- the sealed leaf carries a CT Precertificate SCT whose Log ID base64 equals the ctlogs keyId, and stripping ctlogs from a copy of the trusted root makes cosign fail with 'only able to verify 0 SCT entries; unable to meet threshold of 1', so the pass is load-bearing. Exit gates on the sealed (V) layer only: a sealed failure runs exit 1, while the engine-context and informational loop only echoes WARN and cannot alter the recipe exit status. The minimal-invocation measurement the body calls for is recorded in the commit message (--new-bundle-format dropped as deprecated and auto-detected in v3.1.1; --check-claims=false standing in for the synthetic golden subject). Two carried-forward notes: --check-claims=false means the gate does not bind the statement subject to an artifact, which is item-0007's live verify-attestation property; and the acceptance names a Makefile target that item-0097 will delete, so it needs repointing when that lands.

item-0011.final_summary: Landed as commit 3dd5a9d. strike verify now reconstructs the precertificate the CT log signed -- the leaf TBSCertificate with the SCT list extension removed, prefixed by the sha256 of the issuer SubjectPublicKeyInfo -- and checks the log ECDSA signature over it offline, per RFC 6962 3.2, in a new internal/verify/sct.go behind the ErrSCT sentinel. Exactly one SCT is required rather than a threshold of one. ADR-053 is implemented for both transparency logs: the CT key is bound to the SCT own timestamp inside the signed structure, the Rekor key to the RFC3161 trusted time, because Rekor v2 signs no time of its own. Leaf returns the issuing certificate alongside the leaf so both layers rest on one chain build. The trusted-root CUE replica hoists a shared #TransparencyLogReplica projected by both tlogs and ctlogs, carrying both validity bounds. All three golden bundles still verify with enforcement active, and a new TestGoldenCTMutations rejects each of an unknown log id, a key that did not sign the SCT, and a window excluding it. Three notes for whoever works this code next. First, ctlogs is enforced in Go by ParseTrustedRoot, not by lane validation: a lane declaring an inline trustRoot with no ctlogs block still passes strike validate and fails closed later at verify time. That is an instance of the general CUE list required-ness gap, absorbed into item-0016. Second, Inclusion sat at exactly the gocyclo ceiling of 15 before this change, so the two new guards live behind checkpointUnderTrustedKey rather than inline; the function is at the ceiling again and the next layer added to it will trip the gate. Third, the ephemeral instruction for this run omitted its own CUE schema step while requiring the file in its acceptance gates, and its withinWindow grep criterion counted three lines where the definition doc comment makes four; both were reported rather than worked around.

item-0015.final_summary: Retired without implementation, superseded by ADR-051 D5. The item framed deploy-path SSH as a peer permission: lift the not-implemented guard and give deploy containers the run path's mediated SSH and per-step trust delivery. ADR-051 D5 removed the custom method and made rsync, scp, sftp and git over SSH a deploy method of its own, the transport family, with its own Layer V parts (payload from the digest pin, verified host key plus allowlisted protocol observed, step attribution, optional remote post-state capture per D7). The two methods that exist, registry and kubernetes, have no SSH use case, so lifting the guard on its own would grant a kubectl or capture container the front's git-only allowlist with no method behind it. The gate the item named was also wrong: item-0003 rehosts DoT and TLS, while the actual prerequisite is the ADR-038 D1 protocol allowlist extension (sftp subsystem, rsync --server, scp -t/-f), which no item owns. The surviving content -- per-step SSH trust delivery to a deploy container and deploy-side observed records -- belongs inside the transport-family method item when that method is wanted, with the D1 extension and item-0002's allowlisted-command record field as its blockers.

The exhaustive search over host-write calls in both function and method form returns exactly one production site, the compare subcommand writing an operator-named digest file, and a forbidigo rule fails the build if a scratch mechanism reappears. The live registry-deploy lane runs with the process temp directory pointed at an empty directory and leaves it empty; that half observes residue, not transient writes, which the analyzer half rules out. item-0136.final_summary: Landed as b28a8b2. The mediator proxy is bound to its serve context: cancellation closes both connections, so a blocked copy returns and Serve returns promptly even with an in-flight proxied connection open, and the Close doc comment now describes that. Capsule Stop claims the state transition and releases its mutex before the serve-group wait, so one connection that will not close no longer blocks the lifecycle. The engine force-removes a container it created but could not carry to a clean exit, on a context detached from the one that just expired, and returns an empty id afterwards, so a non-empty id names a container that exists; the run path's deferred removal is detached for the same reason. cmdRun is fatal-free and returns its error to main, so capsule stop and trust-volume removal run before a failed run exits non-zero. Three regression tests cover the properties: mediator cancel with an open proxy, engine wait aborted forcing a remove, and a deploy capture unit that hits its step deadline while holding a mediated connection. The mediator integration test lost its drain workaround. Production mutex count unchanged at seven; the lock-free conversion arc was not entered. Two instruction defects surfaced and are recorded in the commit body: an unlisted same-package test caller of allocateMediatedPorts, and an insertion anchor specified as a bare func line that detached the runContainer doc comment.
